title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck defines an 'ordinary stratification of type I' of a space X, where I is an ordered set. It is a map i ↦ X_i into closed subsets satisfying three axioms. (Strat 1): the X_i are closed and form a locally finite family. (Strat 2): i ≤ j ⇒ X_i ⊂ X_j. (Strat 3): X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{k ≤ i,j} X_k. He then notes that the closed strata give a semi-simplicial resolution over flags and a spectral sequence H^p(I, i ↦ H^q(X_i,F)) ⇒ H^*(X,F). Because the closed strata are complicated, he passes to open strata.

This page:
(90) defines the open strata X_i^* = X_i \ ∪_{j<i} X_j. The non-empty ones form a partition of X. In modern terms, each x has a unique smallest index s(x) with x ∈ X_{s(x)}: local finiteness makes the set of indices i with x ∈ X_i finite, and Strat 3 makes it down-directed, so it has a least element. Then X_i^* = s^{-1}(i).

Optional axioms:
- (Strat 4, fidelity): every X_i^* is non-empty, i.e. s is surjective. It is not stable under restriction to an open subset.
- (Strat 4 bis, 'canonicity of I'): every X_i^* is connected and non-empty. This is stronger and even less stable under restriction. With it, I is recovered intrinsically from X as the set of strata.
- (Strat 5, density): X_i^* is dense in X_i, i.e. X_i is the closure of X_i^*. Paraphrased: for j < i, X_j is 'not dense' in X_i. This is stable under restriction to open sets.
- Marginal note: given Strat 5, fidelity is equivalent to X_i ≠ ∅ for all i.

He declares that Strat 4, 4 bis and 5 will only be assumed when explicitly stated.

(91): X_i = ∪_{j ≤ i} X_j^*, i.e. X_i = s^{-1}(↓i).

This prepares the next page. There, for J ⊂ I one sets X_J^* = s^{-1}(J); it commutes with unions and intersections, is closed when J is closed (a down-set), open when J is open, and locally closed for 'bands' (convex subsets). In modern language this says exactly that s : X → I is continuous for the Alexandrov topology on I, with down-sets closed. This is the current definition of a poset-stratified space (Lurie HA A.5; Haine; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka). Here fidelity means surjectivity of s, and density means the order on I is recovered from closure relations among strata.
errors: The gloss of Strat 5, 'j<i ⇒ X_j non dense dans X_i', is inaccurate if read literally. X_i^* is dense in X_i iff ∪_{j<i} X_j (a locally finite union of closed sets) has empty interior in X_i, i.e. each X_j (j<i) is nowhere dense ('rare') in X_i. Counterexample to the literal reading: X_i = [0,2], X_j = [0,1] is not dense in X_i, yet X_i^* = (1,2] is not dense.

The claim that the non-empty X_i^* partition X tacitly needs X = ∪_i X_i, which Strat 1–3 do not state. Uniqueness of the minimal index uses local finiteness (finitely many indices at a point) together with Strat 3.
Minor: the marginal equivalence (fidelity ⇔ all X_i non-empty, under Strat 5) is correct. The implication X_i ≠ ∅ ⇒ X_i^* ≠ ∅ uses X_i = closure of X_i^*.

ideas.what: Open strata X_i^* = X_i minus the smaller closed strata, giving a partition of X indexed by I; equivalently a map s: X → I with X_i = s^{-1}(↓i)
ideas.modern_name: poset-stratified space (continuous map to a poset with Alexandrov topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; formalized in Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A.5 (c. 2012–17), Haine, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts; Esquisse d'un programme §5 only sketches tame stratified spaces informally

ideas.what: Fidelity axiom (every open stratum non-empty), noted as not stable under restriction to opens
ideas.modern_name: surjectivity of the stratification map / no empty strata

ideas.what: Canonicity axiom: connected non-empty open strata, so that the index poset is intrinsic
ideas.modern_name: stratification by connected strata; poset of strata ordered by closure

ideas.what: Density axiom: closed stratum = closure of open stratum; stable under restriction to opens
ideas.modern_name: frontier-type condition / closure of each stratum is a union of strata indexed by ↓i

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatics (poset-indexed closed strata with Strat 3, open strata as s^{-1}(i), with sets X_J^* behaving like preimages of Alexandrov-open/closed sets) is essentially the modern definition of a poset-stratified space as a continuous map to I with the Alexandrov topology. He also separates fidelity (surjectivity) and density as optional axioms, distinguishing them by stability under restriction to opens. This anticipates by roughly 30 years the formalism used in Lurie's exit-path ∞-categories and later work, but the content is foundational bookkeeping rather than a new result.
missed.quote: (Strat 5) (densité) ∀i∈I, X_i^* dense dans X_i ... Cet axiome a l'avantage d'être stable par restriction à un ouvert.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck's 1981–82 choice of poset-indexed (rather than filtration-indexed) stratifications, aligned with current homotopy-theoretic practice.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard foundational definitions: open strata, fidelity, connectedness and density axioms. Their poset-indexed form anticipates modern conventions, but nothing here is a non-trivial unpublished result.
transcription_corrections: The left-margin note reads: 'moyennant (Strat 5), la condition de fidélité équivaut à ∀i∈I X_i≠∅ (car X_i = \overline{X_i^*} donc X_i≠∅ ⇒ X_i^*≠∅)'. The isolated '{+(Strat 5)+}' inserted after Strat 4 bis belongs to this marginal note, not to the Strat 4 bis line.
The interlinear 'i.e. X_i = \overline{X_i^*}' is attached to Strat 5 (density), not to Strat 4 bis.
Strat 4 bis reads: 'les X_i^* sont connexes non vides' (the line break splits 'connexes' / 'non vides').
The crossed-out heading is approximately 'Stratifications non fidèles ... implique' (illegible); the transcription's guess is unreliable.
The final line may read 'donc on a, si i, j ∈ J' rather than '∈ I' (ambiguous in the image).
